components.name: Search Field
components.description: Search by name or meaning; '/' focuses it.
components.html: <label class="ds-search"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><circle cx="11" cy="11" r="8"/><path d="m21 21-4.3-4.3"/></svg><input placeholder="Search: a name, or what the code does"><kbd>/</kbd></label>
components.css: .ds-search{position:relative;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;height:36px;padding:0 9px 0 11px;background:var(--paper,#f7f6f2);border:1px solid var(--rule,#dddbd4);border-radius:6px;color:var(--ink-muted,#565b62);font:400 14px/1.45 'Archivo Variable',system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-search input{flex:1;border:0;background:none;font:inherit;color:var(--ink,#17191c);outline:none}.ds-search:focus-within{outline:2px solid var(--focus,#17191c)}.ds-search kbd{font:600 12px/1 'JetBrains Mono',monospace;border:1px solid var(--rule,#dddbd4);border-radius:4px;padding:3px 6px}

components.name: Station Sign
components.description: Header of the function panel: line bullet, name, file and lines, close.
components.css: .ds-sign{display:grid;grid-template-columns:22px 1fr auto;gap:12px;padding:16px;background:var(--panel,#fff);border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule,#dddbd4);font-family:'Archivo Variable',system-ui,sans-serif;color:var(--ink,#17191c)}.ds-bullet{width:22px;height:22px;border-radius:50%;background:#0b4fa8;margin-top:2px}.ds-sign h2{margin:0;font-size:20px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.015em}.ds-sign p{margin:4px 0 0;font-size:12px;color:var(--ink-muted,#565b62)}.ds-sign button{width:32px;height:32px;border:1px solid var(--rule,#dddbd4);border-radius:6px;background:none;cursor:pointer}.ds-sign button:hover{background:var(--hover,#efede7)}.ds-sign button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus,#17191c);outline-offset:2px}

narrative.overview: Cartograph shows a codebase the way a metro diagram shows a city: neighbourhoods of code are coloured lines, functions are stations, calls are track. The map is the work area and owns the screen; the interface around it is ink on paper, quiet enough that the line colours carry the meaning. Density is high and calm: small type, tabular numbers, thin rules, no decoration that does not explain the code.
keyCharacteristics: Enamel line colours belong to neighbourhoods only, never to controls.
Stations: a coloured ring around a paper-coloured centre; a file's top-level code is a solid stop; size grows with calls.
One workhorse grotesk (Archivo) with tabular numerals; JetBrains Mono only for code.
Semantic zoom: file names are landmarks when zoomed out, function names when zoomed in.
Two modes: exploring shows the full-colour transit map; picking a function turns the map grey and lights its route in yellow, the only yellow on screen.

rules.name: The Lines Are Not Buttons Rule
rules.body: Line colours mark neighbourhoods. Controls, links and focus never use them, so a colour on screen always means "this code belongs here".

rules.name: The Yellow Route Rule
rules.body: Yellow means one thing: where you are going. It appears only on a picked station, its direct connections and the track between them (and, later, the agent's route). No line, control or label is ever yellow or amber.

rules.name: The Fade, Don't Delete Rule
rules.body: Showing a route turns everything else to Map Grey; focusing a line fades the rest to Faded Track. Nothing disappears from the map.

rules.name: The Four Sizes Rule
rules.body: 12, 14, 17 and 20px are the whole scale. A new level is a weight or case change, not a new size.

rules.name: The Paper Map Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from tone and hairlines. A shadow means "this floats over the map", nothing else.

dos: Do name a line after its busiest station and show that station's file beneath.
Do switch the map to grey with a yellow route when a function is picked, and restore colours when it is closed.
Do keep every number on screen traceable to the index or a measurement.
Do give every map label a halo in the map colour.
Do reach every function by keyboard through search or the connection lists.
donts: Don't use a line colour on a button, link or focus state.
Don't use yellow or amber anywhere except the route.
Don't add type sizes beyond the four in the scale.
Don't add shadows to surfaces that don't float over the map.
Don't use purple gradients, pill-shaped buttons, emoji icons, invented metrics or filler copy (owner's standing rules).
